name: phone
description: bia's own phone line when bia runs on a phone: SMS in and out (chats phone:<number>), phone calls (ring, answer, reject, place), USSD codes and the line's status (SIM, carrier, roaming, signal). Incoming SMS arrive like other chats; say(channel='phone:+34…') sends an SMS. An incoming call arrives as [incoming call]; a missed one as [missed call]. In a call bia hears the other side (their speech arrives as messages on the phone:<number> chat) and say() on that chat speaks into the call, as in WhatsApp calls; text spoken in a call is not also sent as SMS. On this phone, machine poweroff and reboot switch off or restart the phone itself (Android shuts down cleanly; bia comes back with it on a reboot). Starts by itself when the bia app on the phone has linked the line (files/phone/link.json).
examples: +34625640810|phone:+34625640810|<issued>|<delivered>|hi, are you there? -> say(identity='+34625640810', channel='phone:+34625640810', message='Yes, here!')
root|console|<issued>|<delivered>|text my wife +34600000000 that I am late -> say(identity='+34600000000', channel='phone:+34600000000', message='I am running late.', new_chat=true)
root|console|<issued>|<delivered>|is the SIM in roaming? -> phone_status()
+34625640810|phone:+34625640810|<issued>|<delivered>|[speech en] hello, can you hear me? -> say(identity='+34625640810', channel='phone:+34625640810', message='Yes, I hear you!')
